    def _rescale_private_initialization(tower, input_width, template_widths,

        """Match retained weights' marginal variance without drawing weights.

        and zero biases before slicing. A sliced coefficient retains variance
        2/(template fan_in + template fan_out). Multiply by the square root of
        template fan-sum / actual fan-sum to get dimension-specific variance.
        A shallow readout comes from the original final affine, hence its
        source fan-sum is template_widths[-1]+1 even though it now reads the
        first hidden layer. This does not restore the removed layer/function.
        Dice alpha/running buffers, biases and all residual weights are intact.
        This constructor-only operation adds no prediction-time arithmetic.
        """

            return

            raise ValueError('Expected shallow or deep inherited private tower')

        with torch.no_grad():
            if hidden_scale == 'xavier':
                for index, linear in enumerate(linears[:-1]):
                    source_sum = source_inputs[index] + template_widths[index]
                    actual_sum = linear.in_features + linear.out_features
                    linear.weight.mul_((source_sum / actual_sum) ** 0.5)
            if readout_scale == 'xavier':
                output = linears[-1]
                source_sum = template_widths[-1] + 1
                actual_sum = output.in_features + output.out_features
                output.weight.mul_((source_sum / actual_sum) ** 0.5)

    @staticmethod
    def _reduce_tower(tower, widths):
        """Fixed channel subnetwork of a fresh, untrained random template.

        Clone slices so a reduced Parameter owns only its reduced storage.
        Unchanged modules keep their original Parameter objects. The retained
        random weights use the original Xavier scale; no rescaling is applied.
        Initialization scale remains a stated alternative to capacity effects.
        This constructor helper is never called during forward or training.
        """
        previous = tower[0].in_features
        with torch.no_grad():
            for index, hidden in enumerate(widths):

                if not isinstance(linear, nn.Linear) or not isinstance(dice, Dice):
                    raise ValueError('Unexpected parent tower structure')
                if linear.in_features != previous or linear.out_features != hidden:

                        linear.weight[:hidden, :previous].detach().clone(),
                        requires_grad=linear.weight.requires_grad)
                    linear.bias = nn.Parameter(
                        linear.bias[:hidden].detach().clone(),
                        requires_grad=linear.bias.requires_grad)

                        dice.alpha[:hidden].detach().clone(),
                        requires_grad=dice.alpha.requires_grad)

                    output.weight[:, :previous].detach().clone(),

        # positive for every task when historical masks are missing.

            raise ValueError('Released historical task masks are required')
        supplied = inputs[3]
        if isinstance(supplied, (list, tuple)):

                raise ValueError('Wrong number of historical task masks')

                raise ValueError('Expected historical masks with shape [4,B,100]')

    def _compress_both(self, values, mask, auxiliary):

        # Each branch independently covers every valid event exactly once.
        assignment = torch.stack((valid, valid & ~membership, membership), dim=-2)
        assignment = assignment.to(values.dtype).reshape(batch * groups, 3, block_size)

    def _compress_with_match(self, values, mask, auxiliary, match_union):

        external identities, timestamps, state or RNG enter this assignment.
        """

        # count, then unpack to the original valid positions. Invalid

        retain the incumbent gradient paths. Before EACH Dice, rows 3..6

        removes their backward contribution to the preceding affine layer

        batch moments and running-buffer updates at a fixed parameter state.

  "id": "paper:din",
  "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06978v4",
  "version": "content-sha256:5fee25f33f375e51b3ee9417d376ff9dbe2ea3628c932a7679ddfeb0feaaade2",

  "total_lines": 831,
  "start_line": 56,
  "next_line": 111,
  "truncated": false,
  "text": "56: In this way, user features are compressed into a fixed-length representation vector, in regardless of what candidate ads are.
57: The use of fixed-length vector will be a bottleneck, which brings difficulty for Embedding&MLP methods to capture user’s diverse interests effectively from rich historical behaviors.
58: In this paper, we propose a novel model: Deep Interest Network (DIN) which tackles this challenge by designing a local activation unit to adaptively learn the representation of user interests from historical behaviors with respect to a certain ad.
59: This representation vector varies over different ads, improving the expressive ability of model greatly.
60: Besides, we develop two techniques: mini-batch aware regularization and data adaptive activation function which can help training industrial deep networks with hundreds of millions of parameters.
61: Experiments on two public datasets as well as an Alibaba real production dataset with over 2 billion samples demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed approaches, which achieve superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.
62: DIN now has been successfully deployed in the online display advertising system in Alibaba, serving the main traffic.
63: Keywords: Click-Through Rate Prediction, Display Advertising, E-commerce
64: 1. Introduction
65: In cost-per-click (CPC) advertising system, advertisements are ranked by the eCPM (effective cost per mille), which is the product of the bid price and CTR (click-through rate), and CTR needs to be predicted by the system. Hence, the performance of CTR prediction model has a direct impact on the final revenue and plays a key role in the advertising system. Modeling CTR prediction has received much attention from both research and industry community.
66: Recently, inspired by the success of deep learning in computer vision (Huang
67: et al., ) and natural language processing (Bahdanau
68: et al., 2015), deep learning based methods have been proposed for CTR prediction task (Shan
69: et al., ; Covington
70: et al., 2016; Zhai
71: et al., 2016; et al., 2016a).
72: These methods follow a similar Embedding&MLP paradigm: large scale sparse input features are first mapped into low dimensional embedding vectors, and then transformed into fixed-length vectors in a group-wise manner, finally concatenated together to fed into fully connected layers (also known as multilayer perceptron, MLP) to learn the nonlinear relations among features.
73: Compared with commonly used logistic regression model (Mcmahan
74: et al., 2014), these deep learning methods can reduce a lot of feature engineering jobs and enhance the model capability greatly. For simplicity, we name these methods Embedding&MLP in this paper, which now have become popular on CTR prediction task.
75: However, the user representation vector with a limited dimension in Embedding&MLP methods will be a bottleneck to express user’s diverse interests. Take display advertising in e-commerce site as an example. Users might be interested in different kinds of goods simultaneously when visiting the e-commerce site. That is to say, user interests are diverse. When it comes to CTR prediction task, user interests are usually captured from user behavior data.
76: Embedding&MLP methods learn the representation of all interests for a certain user by transforming the embedding vectors of user behaviors into a fixed-length vector, which is in an euclidean space where all users’ representation vectors are.
77: In other words, diverse interests of the user are compressed into a fixed-length vector, which limits the expressive ability of Embedding&MLP methods.
78: To make the representation capable enough for expressing user’s diverse interests, the dimension of the fixed-length vector needs to be largely expanded.
79: Unfortunately, it will dramatically enlarge the size of learning parameters and aggravate the risk of overfitting under limited data. Besides, it adds the burden of computation and storage, which may not be tolerated for an industrial online system.
80: On the other hand, it is not necessary to compress all the diverse interests of a certain user into the same vector when predicting a candidate ad because only part of user’s interests will influence his/her action (to click or not to click). For example, a female swimmer will click a recommended goggle mostly due to the bought of bathing suit rather than the shoes in her last week’s shopping list.
81: Motivated by this, we propose a novel model: Deep Interest Network (DIN), which adaptively calculates the representation vector of user interests by taking into consideration the relevance of historical behaviors given a candidate ad.
82: By introducing a local activation unit, DIN pays attentions to the related user interests by soft-searching for relevant parts of historical behaviors and takes a weighted sum pooling to obtain the representation of user interests with respect to the candidate ad.
83: Behaviors with higher relevance to the candidate ad get higher activated weights and dominate the representation of user interests.
84: We visualize this phenomenon in the experiment section.
85: In this way, the representation vector of user interests varies over different ads, which improves the expressive ability of model under limited dimension and enables DIN to better capture user’s diverse interests.
86: Training industrial deep networks with large scale sparse features is of great challenge.
87: For example, SGD based optimization methods only update those parameters of sparse features appearing in each mini-batch. However, adding with traditional ℓ2\ell_{2} regularization, the computation turns to be unacceptable, which needs to calculate L2-norm over the whole parameters (with size scaling up to billions in our situation) for each mini-batch. In this paper, we develop a novel mini-batch aware regularization where only parameters of non-zero features appearing in each mini-batch participate in the calculation of L2-norm, making the computation acceptable. Besides, we design a data adaptive activation function, which generalizes commonly used PReLU(He
88: et al., 2015) by adaptively adjusting the rectified point w.r.t. distribution of inputs and is shown to be helpful for training industrial networks with sparse features.
89: The contributions of this paper are summarized as follows:
90: •
91: We point out the limit of using fixed-length vector to express user’s diverse interests and design a novel deep interest network (DIN) which introduces a local activation unit to adaptively learn the representation of user interests from historical behaviors w.r.t. given ads. DIN can improve the expressive ability of model greatly and better capture the diversity characteristic of user interests.
92: •
93: We develop two novel techniques to help training industrial deep networks: i) a mini-batch aware regularizer, which saves heavy computation of regularization on deep networks with huge number of parameters and is helpful for avoiding overfitting, ii) a data adaptive activation function, which generalizes PReLU by considering the distribution of inputs and shows well performance.
94: •
95: We conduct extensive experiments on both public and Alibaba datasets. Results verify the effectiveness of proposed DIN and training techniques. Our code11
96: 1
97: Experiment code on two public datasets is available on GitHub: https://github.com/zhougr1993/DeepInterestNetwork is publicly available. The proposed approaches have been deployed in the commercial display advertising system in Alibaba, one of world’s largest advertising platform, contributing significant improvement to the business.
98: In this paper we focus on the CTR prediction modeling in the scenario of display advertising in e-commerce industry.
99: Methods discussed here can be applied in similar scenarios with rich user behaviors, such as personalized recommendation in e-commerce sites, feeds ranking in social networks etc.
100: The rest of the paper is organized as follows. We discuss related work in section 2 and introduce the background about characteristic of user behavior data in display advertising system of e-commerce site in section 3. Section 4 and 5 describe in detail the design of DIN model as well as two proposed training techniques. We present experiments in section 6 and conclude in section 7.
101: 2. Relatedwork
102: The structure of CTR prediction model has evolved from shallow to deep. At the same time, the number of samples and the dimension of features used in CTR model have become larger and larger. In order to better extract feature relations to improve performance, several works pay attention to the design of model structure.
103: As a pioneer work, NNLM (Bengio Yoshua
104: et al., 2003) learns distributed representation for each word,
105: aiming to avoid curse of dimension in language modeling.
106: This method, often referred to as embedding,
107: has inspired many natural language models and CTR prediction models that need to handle large-scale sparse inputs.
108: LS-PLM (Gai
109: et al., 2017) and FM (Rendle, 2010) models can be viewed as a class of networks with one hidden layer, which first
110: employs embedding layer on sparse inputs and then imposes specially designed transformation functions for target fitting, aiming to capture the combination relations among features."
}
